System description:
# Case: Uber ATG automated test vehicle (Tempe, Arizona, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-19/03. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A modified Volvo XC90 SUV is used by Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG) to test an automated driving system (ADS) on public roads. The ADS is designed to drive the vehicle without human input in defined conditions, up to about 45 mph in this test program.

## Main parts
- Sensors: roof-mounted lidar, radar units and cameras covering the area around the vehicle.
- Perception: detects objects around the vehicle, classifies each one (for example vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, other), and tracks it over time.
- Prediction: estimates where each tracked object will go next, using its class and recent movement.
- Planning and control: chooses a path and speed, and controls steering, throttle and braking.
- Vehicle: the Volvo factory driver-assistance features (such as forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking) are part of the base vehicle.

## People
- One vehicle operator sits in the driver seat. The operator is responsible for watching the road and taking over control when needed. The operator also uses a tablet-style interface to tag events and check system status.
- Other road users share the road: pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers. They are not aware of the test program.

## Operating context
Public multi-lane roads in an urban area, day and night, with posted speed limits, marked crosswalks, intersections and street lighting that varies by location.

Classify detected objects, such as vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles.
Track objects over time.
Estimate where each tracked object will move next using its class and recent movement.
Choose a path and speed for the vehicle.
Control vehicle steering, throttle, and braking.
Provide forward collision warning.
Provide automatic emergency braking.
Watch the road while the ADS is operating.
Take over vehicle control when needed.
Tag events using the tablet-style interface.
Check system status using the tablet-style interface.
Travel and cross roads safely.
Travel on roads safely.
Drive and share the road safely.

requirements.text: The ADS shall retain low-confidence hypotheses for potentially safety-relevant road users and shall plan conservatively around them until sensor evidence confirms they are absent or no longer in a position to affect the vehicle.

The system shall detect when the operator's gaze is away from the road for more than 2 seconds, issue an attention alert, and initiate a safe fallback if the operator does not resume road monitoring within 5 seconds.

The prediction component shall represent multiple plausible future paths for a tracked road user when its next movement is uncertain, and shall provide those paths to planning rather than relying only on the most likely path.

When the time available for intervention is less than the validated operator response time plus control-transfer time and a safety margin, the ADS shall execute a safe fallback without relying on the operator to take over.
The ADS shall monitor whether sensor coverage is sufficient for safe operation and, when it is not, shall reduce speed or enter a safe fallback before continuing through the affected area.

The tracking component shall mark a track invalid when its age or position uncertainty exceeds configured safety limits, and shall provide planning with the track's possible reachable area until the object is reacquired or confirmed absent.
The ADS shall limit speed so that its calculated stopping distance, including system response delay and current road conditions, does not exceed the verified clear distance ahead.

The planning component shall treat areas reachable by objects under uncertain or incomplete predictions as occupied and shall not select a path through those areas unless sensing confirms they are clear.
The ADS shall detect and track pedestrians whether or not they are at a marked crosswalk, and shall yield or brake when a pedestrian's possible path intersects the vehicle's path.

When another vehicle enters or is predicted to enter the test vehicle's path with insufficient safe separation, the ADS shall promptly apply braking or an available evasive maneuver to reduce collision risk.
